title: Whole prognosis with history-dependent qualification and a repeated delayed inquiry
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED. A complete Hippocratic examination retains the same adverse appearance while prior causes and a day-and-night course alter its warranted prognosis; later examination explicitly reuses the earlier questions.

whole_content_inventory.content: In acute disease examine the countenance first. Similarity to healthy people is favorable, similarity to the patient’s own healthy appearance more favorable; the most opposed appearance is worst.

Retain the full adverse-face description: sharp nose; hollow eyes; collapsed temples; cold contracted ears with turned-out lobes; rough, distended and parched forehead skin; whole-face color green, black, livid or lead-colored.
At disease onset, if that appearance is not accounted for by other symptoms, inquire about prolonged sleeplessness, very loose bowels and lack of food.
If any of those causes is admitted, danger is judged less. A day and night makes apparent whether the countenance arose from these causes. Reduced danger does not mean guaranteed survival.

The two written if-clauses concern none of those causes being reported and symptoms not subsiding in the aforementioned interval, followed by imminent-death prognosis. Their exact conjunction/scope is not silently resolved from this English translation.

At the more advanced third or fourth day with the same appearance, repeat the same inquiries and attend to other signs on the whole face, body and eyes. This is a genuine backward procedural reference, not a new independent question list.

Keep every further adverse sign: eyes shunning light, involuntary tears, squint, unequal size, red or livid whites or black veins, gum, restlessness, protrusion or marked hollowness; a squalid dark countenance or changed whole-face color. The passage calls these bad and fatal.

Observe eyes during sleep: exposed white because lids do not close, with written exclusions mentioning diarrhea, medicinal purgation and the patient’s habitual sleep appearance. Preserve the printed and/or connective ambiguity; do not silently replace it with a medical rule preferred by the analyst.
Contracted, livid or pale eyelid, lip or nose together with some other signs entails imminent death in the source’s historical claim.
The final separate assertion calls relaxed, pendent, cold and blanched lips a mortal sign. Do not omit it merely because the first temporal contrast supplied the proposed discriminator.

design.hypothesis: A whole passage may be a diagnostic discourse that compares observations to a baseline, asks about alternative antecedent causes, qualifies a judgment, and reuses the inquiry after a stated interval/stage. This is a content hypothesis, not a claim about the manuscript.
design.composition_policy: The same patient, appearance and query-bundle references persist across the first judgment, reassessment and later repetition. Conditional antecedent, inquiry result and prognosis are different types. This finite conceptual inventory is not a selected surface grammar.
design.coupled_consequence: The same adverse face can support a lesser-danger judgment when an alternative cause is admitted, while the interval supplies further evidential assessment. A later same-inquiries reference must target the previously specified three-cause inquiry, not whichever immediately preceding symptom happens to be nearest.

rivals.rule: One adverse appearance has one unconditional fixed prognosis.
rivals.contrast: Cannot preserve the explicitly lower danger from admitted history while keeping the appearance fixed.

rivals.rule: All clauses are successive treatments or state changes.
rivals.contrast: Asking whether hunger/sleeplessness occurred does not instruct their production; later repetition repeats questions, not all intervening signs.

rivals.rule: An admitted alternative cause guarantees survival.
rivals.contrast: Source says danger is less and requires further course assessment, not survival.

rivals.rule: An unmentioned cause counts as absent.
rivals.contrast: Confessed history and reported absence are explicit evidential alternatives; unknown is retained.

H08: retain literal printed and/or and a possible all-exclusions interpretation as alternatives; no choice made here.
costs_and_symmetries: Full symptom inventory contains many one-off lexical values; no measured compression or automatic target binding is claimed.
Comparative risk is not a binary alive/dead variable.
A generic correctly scoped medical account is a serious rival; a connector frequency cannot distinguish it.
Baseline appearance of this patient differs from generic healthy people.

predecessors.retained: Generic connectors can accompany opposition; source scope does not identify a target contrast marker.

predecessors.difference: Treatment fallback and ordered polarity differ from repeat-inquiry and temporally qualified prognosis; no old target/gloss is reused.

predecessors.retained: Anaphoric recurrence alone does not bind content; the exact reused inquiry must be supplied jointly in a whole hypothesis.

design.smallest_future_decision: Only after a complete admitted passage and shared writing contract are nominated, ask whether the same represented sign/history relation recurs with the predicted changed judgment and exact query reuse. The present source acquisition is not that test.
design.likely_failure: Translation-scope uncertainty or many free symptom values may make the whole content underdetermined; no target owner or surface writer is supplied.

source_evidence.quote: ## A. A visible sign can retain its identity while its prognosis changes

source.work: Hippocratic Prognostic, complete Internet Classics Archive Part 2
source.historical_date: Ancient Greek work, conventionally around400BCE as the institutional host labels it; precise authorship/date and a medieval Latin witness are not established here.
source.witness: Francis Adams English translation (1849 tradition), MIT Internet Classics Archive digital text. This task owns this complete English section, not a Greek manuscript or medieval Latin wording.
source.catalog_limit: Perseus catalog identifies Adams,1886 printing, originally1849; it does not prove the exact print exemplar used by the MIT page.
source.normalization: HTML text only, whitespace collapsed, one final newline; whole Part2 bounded from He should observe thus to lips ... blanched. No OCR or image inspection.
source_ambiguities: The paired if-clauses before imminent death do not receive an unannounced Boolean connective.
The eyelid passage prints and/or around diarrhea, medicinal purgation and habit. A Greek/edition collation is required before a unique truth table is selected.
The source’s comparative danger, fatal, very deadly and imminent-death judgments are not collapsed to one binary output.
Healthy-person comparison and this patient’s own healthy baseline are distinct.
Historical prognoses are source claims, not current medical guidance.
